About

Size Em Up!

How to Play

Tap a topic to open it
Solo Game

Tap Solo Game from Home to choose Daily Challenge, Monthly Challenge, Worlds, Quick Game or Survival. Quick Game starts with 3 Medium bots, with no room code or waiting on other people. You can add more bots, remove extras, or choose Low, Medium or High bot accuracy in the lobby before you begin. Solo games are always free, even before Party Mode is unlocked.

Round XP depends on your opponents: Low accuracy ×0.8, Medium accuracy or people ×1.1, and High accuracy ×1.2. Mixed lobbies average the opponents who submitted a guess. XP already earned stays unchanged. Game-completion XP and Daily, Worlds, Monthly and Survival XP keep their usual rates.

Hosting a party

Tap Party Mode, then pick a mode (Classic Party, or Team vs Team to play 2v2) to choose the room settings and what happens if you disconnect, then tap Create Room. Next, pick your name and avatar and tap Join Lobby - you're the host, so only you can start the game once everyone's in. If you've saved a preset (see Host settings below), tap one of the three preset slots above the settings to load it instantly.

Joining a room

Tap Join Game, type the 4-letter room code the host gave you, and tap Continue. Then pick your name and avatar and tap Join Lobby. Every player needs a unique avatar per room, so any already taken will be grayed out.

Rejoining a room

If you get disconnected or reload mid-game, open Join Game - your most recent room shows up as Last game with a one-tap Rejoin button.

Host settings

All chosen once, up front, before the room is created:

If host disconnects - "Give another player host" auto-hands host duties to whoever's been in the room longest if you drop; "Save my host spot" holds your spot so rejoining under the same name gets it back.

Timer - how many seconds each round's guessing phase lasts. Rounds - how many rounds the game runs. Item selection - see next section.

Round advance - Auto Mode moves everyone on to the next screen by itself after the "Auto-advance delay," so no one has to tap anything. Manual Host Mode instead waits for the host to tap Next, which is handy if you want to talk through an answer before moving on. The host can flip this mode on the fly mid-game too, from the toggle next to the timer.

Presets - once you've got settings you like, save them from Settings > Custom Game Presets into one of three slots with its own name and icon, so you can load the whole setup again next time instead of re-entering it.

Item selection

Anything goes pairs any two objects at random, so you might get wildly mismatched sizes. Keep it relative only pairs objects where the smaller one is at least 15% of the larger one's size, so you won't be asked how many grains of sand long the Eiffel Tower is.

How sizes are measured

Every object uses whatever dimension you'd naturally measure it by in real life, not just whichever number happens to be biggest.

Anything naturally low and horizontal - like a fire truck or an ant - is measured by its length (bumper-to-bumper, nose-to-tail), not how tall it stands. Anything naturally tall and upright - like a giraffe or a skyscraper - is measured by height instead.

Questions name the dimension being compared: length, height, width, diameter, depth, wingspan, or edge length. Extra wording tells you when a cord, tail, pedestal, or post is included. Wired earbuds include the full cord; the wireless earbuds case is measured on its own. A tied necktie is measured from knot to tip.

Power-ups

Available in Quick Game, Worlds, and Survival. Tap an available power-up to use it immediately for the displayed coin price. There is no confirmation pop-up. Unaffordable power-ups are dimmed.

Use rerolls, buffer, and reveal before submitting. In Quick Game, you can still add a buffer while waiting, before Second Chance begins. Only 50/50 is available during Second Chance. Used power-ups stay in their places, greyed out and marked Used; only one reroll is allowed per question.

Worlds and Survival stay untimed and have no Second Chance. A reroll does not add a timer. Power-ups are unavailable in Party, Daily, and Monthly challenges, including practice.

Second chances

Every round, after guesses lock, everyone gets a few seconds to either pick another answer (if you think it's right) - one of the answers on the table is secretly the real answer, and picking it earns a bonus point, or double down on your own guess. Doubling down adds a bonus to your own points if your guess turns out to be the closest.

Scoring

Only the single closest guess each round scores: +3 points normally, or +5 if it's within 0.9 of the exact answer. Everyone else gets 0 for that round, no matter how close they were.

Second-chance bonus: +1 if you didn't win the round and you picked the hidden card, the real answer. Picking the winner's answer earns nothing, and the round's winner doesn't collect it. It only shows up when two or more players guessed (and not if someone guessed the exact answer). Players who picked an answer show up beside it, and the answer picked the most can earn a crowd favorite point.

Double down: if your own guess is the round's closest, doubling down adds a flat +2 on top - as long as someone else guessed that round too, so it can't be earned for free in a solo practice game with no bots.

Crowd favorite: +1 to whoever got 2 or more second-chance picks that round (whichever count is highest), whether or not their answer was actually closest. Ties (even 3-way or more) all get it.

"Spot On!" (within 1% of the answer) and "Perfect!" (within 0.005) are just on-screen recognition, not extra points.

At the very end of the game, the top 3 players by average accuracy get a one-time bonus: +10 / +6 / +3. Calculate accuracy separately for each round, then average those percentages. Overestimates and underestimates never cancel each other out.

Accuracy & Survival

Accuracy starts at 100%. Subtract how far your guess is from the answer, as a percentage of that answer. Accuracy stays between 0% and 100%.

For an answer of 100, guessing 75 is 75% accurate and guessing 150 is 50% accurate. Across those two rounds, your average accuracy is 62.5%. A very large miss earns 0%, never a negative percentage.

Examples for an answer of 10: guess 11 is 90%, guess 12 is 80%, guess 8 is 80%, guess 7 is 70%, guess 5 is 50%, and guess 0 or 20 is 0%.

The marks you see on results: a green check is 90% or better, a yellow check is 70% to 89%, an orange X is 40% to 69%, and a red X is under 40%.

Survival: you have 3 lives. A guess under 60% accurate costs one, and the game ends when they're gone. For an answer of 10, anything from 6 up to 14 keeps you safe. Questions get trickier the longer you last, and your score is how many rounds you survive. The % beside your hearts is your running average accuracy for the run.

Tiebreakers

During the game, tied scores just stay tied - same medal, no resolution needed. In the final results, a tied score is broken by whoever has the higher average accuracy; if that's tied too, both receive the win. Completed rounds count toward stats and object discovery even if you leave early; only a finished game counts as a game played or won.

Objects & collections

Open Stats > Objects from the top toolbar to see every object that can show up in a round, grouped alphabetically - ones you haven't seen yet show as a locked "????" row. The stat boxes at the top track how many objects you've discovered and how many different pairings you've been asked to compare, with a Hide Undiscovered toggle to see only what you've found so far.

The Monthly tab (next to Objects) holds seasonal items, like Christmas or Halloween props, in a pack for each month. Each one is free to use during its real-world month - the current month's category is highlighted with a "Currently Active" tag - and outside that window it shows "Back in <Month>" unless you've bought that pack (or the Yearly Object Sampler Pack) from the Shop to keep it in rotation all year.

Your avatar collection works the same way: open it from the View All Avatars button on the Shop's Avatars tab to see every avatar grouped by rarity, with a Discovered count and its own Hide Undiscovered toggle.

Awards

Tap the Awards icon in the toolbar to see achievements across categories - Collector, Accuracy, Winning, Second chance, Social, Fun, Worlds, Monthly, and Fantasy - each with a few tiers that get harder (and pay out more coins) as you go. A red dot on the toolbar icon means you've got a reward ready to claim; tap the achievement to collect its coins. A Hide Completed toggle keeps the list focused on what's still in progress.

The Fantasy awards are different: instead of coins, each one unlocks a mythical creature or other make-believe friend, like a goblin, dragon, mermaid, alien or flying saucer. Unlocked creatures can pop up as objects in Host Party and Quick Game rounds (when the host has unlocked them), and never in Daily, Monthly, Worlds or Survival challenges. Once you've seen one in a round, it shows up in your Objects list with the rest. Unlock 20 of them and the Make Believe world opens in Worlds, packed with all of them.

Good to know

Bots can be added from the lobby (Low, Medium or High accuracy) if you want to practice solo or fill out a small group. Reactions are little animated pictures you can send from the bar along the bottom at any time during a game (except the reveal animation). Flairs are the burst of effects (hearts, fireworks, snow...) that plays around your card for everyone to see when you win a round - equip one from Style. The host can Pause to freeze the timer, and either the host or a player can Exit at any time.

Play immediately as a guest. Welcome to Size Em Up! automatically gives you 100 coins when your profile is established. Connecting Google is optional: the separate Account Connected achievement automatically adds 50 coins the first time. Both appear in Awards and pay only once.

Signing in with Google (Settings > Account) saves your coins, avatars, and unlocks to your account instead of just this device, so you can pick up where you left off on a new phone. A new account inherits your guest progress and reward history. If the account already has progress, its saved progress takes precedence. Reopening the game or signing in again does not repeat either starter reward.

Progress and playing again

Use Stats for Games won, finished games, win rate, accuracy and records. Choose a mode to see Worlds stars, Survival best runs, or Daily streaks. Accuracy includes power-up adjustments. Accuracy averages include submitted guesses; missed submissions are counted separately.

Worlds award stars above 60%, 75%, and 90%. Earn 13 stars in a World to claim its home screen in Awards or on the World page, and all 15 stars for mastery. Survival keeps you safe at 60% or above. Worlds and Survival offer Resume for unfinished attempts.

In a party lobby, mark yourself Ready and check the room rules. After the final results, each player collects their own coins. The host can then start a rematch with the same group or leave.

Settings offers effects volume, reduced motion and larger menu text. Object search uses the game's keyboard; tap Done to minimize it.

The Shop

Your score becomes coins when a game ends, win or lose. Open Shop for coins, offers, and monthly packs. Open Style for avatars, reactions, flairs, boards, backgrounds, and home screens:

Shop - buy coin packs (or watch an ad for a few free coins), unlock unlimited Party Mode games for good, and pick up monthly object packs to keep seasonal objects in the mix year-round.

Avatars - each Pull costs 50 coins and unlocks a random avatar you don't already have. Rarer avatars (Rare, Ultra-rare) show up less often than Common ones. Tap View All Avatars to see every avatar grouped by rarity, with locked ones grayed out.

Style - buy and equip Reaction packs and Flair packs here; whatever you've equipped is what shows up in games.
